raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t chase fancy methods. I do this the way we’ve done here for years, but I still watch what happens in the village. My land is only 16.9 mu, so I can’t gamble. Wheat and maize together are the safest for me. If wheat is decent, I have grain and money. If maize does well after that, the year is steady.

For wheat, I won’t cut fertilizer too hard, because if wheat turns yellow in spring, yield drops fast and I can’t make that back later. But I also won’t spend too much at once. I’ll use a base dressing first, then topdress once in spring. Water from the well costs money, so I’ll irrigate at the important times, not too many times. For maize, the main thing is to plant quickly after wheat harvest. Around here everybody knows that if you delay maize, yield falls. I’ll use hybrid maize seed like most neighbors do, put on enough fertilizer for a stable crop, and water once or twice depending on rain. At my age, I rely mostly on family labor, and if the wheat harvest and maize sowing are too tight, I’ll hire a little machine help rather than miss the window.
